notes: Includes strip mine reclamation area averaged over plant lifetime. Underground mining gives lower direct footprint but higher subsidence area.
Conventional gas fields have very small footprint per MWh; unconventional (shale) well pads + access roads + pipelines push the p95 up substantially.
Includes reactor site, cooling infrastructure, and uranium mining footprint averaged over lifetime. Excludes geological repository area (negligible on a per-MWh basis).
Utility-scale ground-mount PV, project area (fenceline). Actual panel coverage is ~30-50%% of project area; the rest is inter-row spacing and setbacks. Rooftop PV has effectively zero land use.
Project boundary (lease area). Direct footprint (turbine pads, access roads, substation) is only 1-3%% of project area — the rest remains in agricultural or grazing use.
Reservoir surface area normalised per MWh. Run-of-river: near zero. Large storage reservoirs (e.g. Churchill Falls, Itaipu): moderate. Shallow tropical reservoirs (Tucurui): very high.
Dedicated energy crops (switchgrass, miscanthus). The largest footprint of any energy source by a wide margin — a single 500 MW biomass plant needs ~1,500 km2 of cropland.
Resource-dependent. Flash plants in volcanic fields (Geysers, Larderello) are compact; EGS plants with multiple wells spread out more.
